decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to the basket with open gripper, raising and pitching toward a top grasp while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Advance above the rear egg in the left basket, gradually orienting the gripper downward; right arm remains parked.
Align the open left fingers over the rear egg, approaching vertically with conservative descent.
Lower around the rear egg, correcting slightly forward; leave the fingers open until the egg is between them.
Center the rear egg between the fingers, close fully, then begin a short vertical lift to check retention visually.
Lift the retained egg clear of the basket rim, then start translating toward the holder while keeping the gripper fully closed.
Carry the first egg toward the holder's left column above rim height; retain the same downward grasp orientation.
Tracking shows reach strain near the center. Keep the left wrist on its side, tilt the held egg toward the holder, and ease backward and downward to regain margin.
Replan from the measured wrist pose with small increments, bringing the retained egg over the rear-left cup and reducing height.
The wrist is not following the inward target. Retract toward the robot and tilt the grasp forward to relieve reach constraints before another placement approach.
Approach the rear-left cup with the wrist kept left of center, using the angled gripper to carry the egg over the cup.
Keep the wrist in the left workspace and angle the retained egg inward, reducing the forward offset before lowering into the cup.
The egg appears near the open lid edge. Move back and lower to clear that edge before shifting farther over the holder.
Retreat backward and upward from the lid-side obstruction with the egg retained, establishing clearance for a frontward placement approach.
Now clear of the lid, move the retained egg over the front-left cup with the wrist left of center and begin a shallow descent.
Lower the egg toward the front-left cup with a slight backward correction to stay clear of the partially tilted lid.
The egg is visibly in the front-left cup. Open and withdraw leftward/upward to leave it seated and clear the holder.
The lid has fallen closed early. Prepare the right arm to reopen its front edge while the empty left arm moves back over the basket.
Bring the right open fingertips toward the lid's front tab; continue reorienting the left gripper above the basket without contacting eggs.
Approach the closed lid's front tab with the right fingers and lower the left open gripper toward the front egg, maintaining separate workspaces.
Try gripping and lifting the lid's front edge with the right arm; lower the left fingers around the next egg without closing yet.
The holder is open and one egg is visible inside. Withdraw the right arm; close the left gripper around the front basket egg and test a short lift.
The second egg was not retained. Reopen and descend farther around its sides; keep the right arm clear of the now-open holder.
Correct the left fingertips backward over the front egg, narrowing the opening slightly to avoid its neighbors before the final descent.
Set the fingers lower around the front egg, close fully, and test retention with a short lift.
The fingers closed above the egg rather than retaining it. Reopen and insert farther down around its sides, with a small backward correction.
Reset to a nearly vertical grasp over the front egg, lifting briefly to clear neighboring eggs before realigning.
Descend vertically around the centered front egg, close fully, then lift slightly to verify retention.
Lift the candidate second grasp above the basket, keeping the fingers fully closed and watching for the egg to rise with them.
The egg remained in the basket. Recenter on its new visible position and lower the fully open gripper vertically for a better-aligned grasp.
Insert the open fingers lower around the centered egg and close at that depth, delaying lift until the grasp is visually checked.
The wrist view shows the egg still behind the pinch center. Reopen, back the gripper over it by a few centimeters, and reseat the fingers.
Close on the now-centered front egg without descending against the basket rim, then lift slowly to check that it is retained.
The egg now rises with the fingers. Lift clear and angle it inward for a rear-left placement without sweeping into the lid.
Carry the retained second egg toward the rear-left cup, keeping its orientation fixed and the wrist on the left side.
Align the second egg farther forward over the rear-left cup and lower toward the holder, avoiding the raised lid.
Release the second egg over the rear-left cup and withdraw diagonally away from the raised lid, checking where the egg settles.
Two eggs are visible in the holder. Return the left gripper toward the nearer remaining basket egg and rotate back toward a top grasp.
Finish the downward orientation and move forward above the rightmost basket egg, maintaining clearance before descending.
Lower the open fingers around the rightmost remaining egg, compensating for the fingertip offset with a slight backward adjustment.
Close around the centered third egg and lift a short distance to verify retention before transporting it.
The third egg slipped forward instead of being retained. Reopen and follow its new position, bringing the pinch center forward while descending.
Shift the open pinch center a little farther forward and left onto the egg's middle, then close without lifting yet.
The egg shifted toward the basket center. Clear the rim, reopen, and recenter leftward and backward over the egg rather than pulling on the basket.
Close around the third egg after a small centering adjustment, then make a gentle test lift.
The third egg is retained between the fingers. Lift clear and angle inward for the holder's empty right column without crossing the wrists.
Approach the empty front-right cup from above and in front, increasing inward tilt while keeping the left wrist left of center and clear of the seated eggs.
Three eggs are now visible in the holder and the left fingers are empty. Open and retreat toward the basket for the last egg.
Return to a downward grasp above the last basket egg, approaching its visible center with the fingers open.
Lower the open gripper toward the last egg with a small forward-left correction to center it between the fingers.
Close around the last egg and lift away from the basket rim, checking that the egg remains between the fingers.
The last egg was not retained. Reopen, recenter leftward on its visible position, and insert the fingers deeper around its sides.
Close on the last egg now between the fingers and lift vertically, easing inward away from the basket rim.
The last egg slipped out. Fully reopen before descending deeper, with a backward correction for the angled fingertips.
Move the pinch center slightly inward and backward onto the egg while clearing the rim, then close without lifting prematurely.
The egg moved backward under the tips. Reopen fully and follow it backward and deeper so the fingers surround its middle rather than its upper edge.
Straighten the approach and turn the open fingers slightly to clear the basket wall, bringing the pinch center backward onto the last egg.
Use a narrower opening to clear the rim and insert the fingertips below the egg's upper edge, then close at the deeper position.
The basket rim is preventing a deep grasp. Reopen and approach the last egg from slightly farther forward with the fingers tilted back, clearing the near rim.
With the rim cleared and the egg centered, lower around its sides, close fully, and make a short retention test lift.
Test the last grasp with a steady lift clear of the basket before beginning the transfer; keep the gripper fully closed.
The last egg is retained. Begin a high transfer toward the remaining cup, gradually rotating inward while maintaining a closed grasp and clearance over the other eggs.
Keep the last grasp orientation steady while carrying above the holder, adding height to clear the three seated eggs.
Align the last egg over the empty rear-right cup while lowering slightly, keeping the wrist left of center and retaining the grasp.
The last egg is above the empty rear-right cup. Lower vertically with the grasp closed, watching the lid and the seated eggs.
The last egg appears to be resting against the lid rather than descending with the fingers. Open and withdraw to remove the obstruction and inspect its settling position.
Clear the left arm away and bring the right open gripper up toward the last egg resting on the lid, to transfer it into the empty rear-right cup.
Advance the right gripper above the rear-right area while pitching downward; retract the left arm to leave the holder unobstructed.
Bring the right open fingers forward and slightly left around the egg resting on the lid, with a gentle descent and a reduced opening to avoid the adjacent egg.
Close the right fingers at the egg and test a short backward/upward withdrawal from the lid; the wrist view is occluded, so retention needs visual confirmation.
